title: Safelisting and Explicit Class Generation
subtopics: Understanding cases where a class is absent from source files
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of safelisting and explicit class generation.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on safelisting and explicit class generation and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: The reliability of safelisting and explicit class generation affects whether Tailwind detects candidate classes and generates the CSS you expect at build time.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Understanding cases where a class is absent from source files; Using @source inline(); Generating selected variants explicitly; Using brace expansion; Avoiding unnecessarily large generated CSS. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to safelisting and explicit class generation, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating safelisting and explicit class generation. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to safelisting and explicit class generation.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to safelisting and explicit class generation.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: The explicitly listed utility is generated even when not discovered in scanned source files.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying safelisting and explicit class generation without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Safelisting and Explicit Class Generation is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
